newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ex-president Salinas's aide called in murder probe.
newsitem.headline: Ex-president Salinas's aide called in murder probe.

text.p: Investigators probing a big political murder in Mexico have called a top aide to former president Carlos Salinas to testify, Attorney General Antonio Lozano Gracia said on Monday.

Lozano's announcement came the day after Mexico's leading weekly news magazine Proceso published what it said were transcripts of a key witness's statement that for the first time suggested the aide -- Salinas's private secretary Justo Ceja -- was in some way connected to machinations surrounding the killing of a top ruling party official.
Asked about Ceja by reporters on Monday, Lozano said: "We have already issued a summons so that he presents himself to testify." He said police were hunting Ceja down to deliver him the summons.

Lozano also seemed to imply that Carlos Salinas -- currently in self-imposed exile in Ireland -- would be asked to give evidence. He said: "We are going to summon everyone ... when someone is not in Mexico there are channels to be able to take a declaration."

Carlos Salinas fled Mexico in disgrace in March 1995 after the economy collapsed and his brother Raul was arrested on charges of masterminding the 1994 killing of Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, secretary-general of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).

Lozano's office also said Raul's former private secretary, Ofelia Calvo, had been arrested on Monday on suspicion of inciting a key witness to retract incriminating evidence he had given against Raul in the Ruiz Massieu case.

Detectives last month found a body buried in the grounds of a Mexico City ranch used by Raul. They are trying to identify the remains to determine whether they belong to a missing politician who may have helped Raul arrange the Ruiz Massieu killing and who was himself murdered afterwards to ensure his silence.
The hitman who has been convicted of pulling the trigger on Ruiz Massieu outside a Mexico City hotel has said in interviews that he was hired for the murder by Munoz Rocha.

But the investigation into Raul's alleged participation in the Ruiz Massieu killing has been hampered by the investigators' inability so far to gather hard evidence. Raul has staunchly denied any involvement and his lawyers claim the body found in the ranch was planted by the police.
